title: No-Bake Cheesecake
subtitle: Cream cheese filling on a biscuit base, set in the fridge
excerpt: A buttered digestive biscuit base topped with a smooth, cream cheese and double cream filling, set overnight in the fridge. No oven required. Topped with fresh berries before serving.

recipe.sourceNotes: No-bake cheesecake sets by chilling rather than baking: the double cream is whipped into the cream cheese mixture and provides structure as it cools. It is firmer and less custardy than a New York baked cheesecake. The British version typically uses digestive biscuits for the base and cream cheese or mascarpone for the filling. Setting overnight gives a firmer, cleaner-slicing result than the minimum four-hour chill, so plan ahead.

content.text: Whip the cream to soft peaks before folding it in: over-whipping makes the filling grainy. Press the biscuit base firmly and evenly into the tin. The filling must be chilled for at least four hours but overnight is better. Run a knife around the edge before releasing the tin sides.
Mix the crushed biscuits with the melted butter. Press firmly into the base of a 23 cm springform tin. Refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Beat the cream cheese, icing sugar, lemon juice, and vanilla until smooth. In a separate bowl, whip the double cream to soft peaks.
Fold the whipped cream into the cream cheese mixture in two additions. Spoon over the biscuit base. Smooth the top with a palette knife or the back of a spoon.
Refrigerate for at least 4 hours, ideally overnight. To serve, run a knife around the edge, release the springform, and top with fresh strawberries.
